answer: Neighborhood Continuity Weighting. Each agent’s influence is scaled by how long its neighbors persist around it, measured as overlap in the quill of recent interaction partners. A new node starts near zero because its counterparties are also new. To gain weight, an attacker must sustain a voyage of interactions through established nodes across multiple epochs, paying real compute and latency per hop. A copycat relic of an old neighbor graph fails because continuity is checked against live, aging edges.
